variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Long-context evaluation measures whether a model can use the right evidence when an input contains many tokens. It varies input length, evidence position, task structure, distractors, and output requirements, then measures both answer quality and whether the answer is supported by the supplied context.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Accepted window
pairs.detail: The tokenizer, API, and serving stack accept the request without truncation or rejection.
pairs.explanation: The tokenizer, API, and serving stack accept the request without truncation or rejection. This is a capacity boundary, not a quality result.

pairs.label: Usable window
pairs.detail: The model meets task and evidence-use thresholds across the tested length and position slices.
pairs.explanation: The model meets task and evidence-use thresholds across the tested length and position slices. This boundary depends on the behavior being evaluated.

pairs.label: Supported frontier
pairs.detail: Quality, grounding, latency, cost, and failure handling pass together for the exact production configuration.
pairs.explanation: Quality, grounding, latency, cost, and failure handling pass together for the exact production configuration. Beyond this frontier, the system must constrain, retrieve, compress, or decompose.

variants.hint:
Accepted window: The tokenizer, API, and serving stack accept the request without truncation or rejection.

Usable window: The model meets task and evidence-use thresholds across the tested length and position slices.

Supported frontier: Quality, grounding, latency, cost, and failure handling pass together for the exact production configuration.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Name the behavior
pairs.detail: Separate single retrieval, multi-document reasoning, global aggregation, long-output generation, and instruction following.
pairs.explanation: Separate single retrieval, multi-document reasoning, global aggregation, long-output generation, and instruction following. Each behavior needs a different ground truth and scorer.

pairs.label: Sweep length and depth
pairs.detail: Place equivalent evidence near the beginning, middle, and end at several context lengths.
pairs.explanation: Place equivalent evidence near the beginning, middle, and end at several context lengths. Repeat with deterministic seeds instead of trusting one placement.

pairs.label: Increase interference
pairs.detail: Add similar entities, stale versions, contradictions, and irrelevant passages.
pairs.explanation: Add similar entities, stale versions, contradictions, and irrelevant passages. Record whether the model cites the controlling source or follows the loudest distractor.

pairs.label: Declare the claim boundary
pairs.detail: Publish slice results and the tested frontier.
pairs.explanation: Publish slice results and the tested frontier. Never convert an untested region into a supported claim by averaging adjacent cells.

pairs.label: Needle-in-a-Haystack
pairs.detail: Insert one known fact at controlled lengths and depths.
pairs.explanation: Insert one known fact at controlled lengths and depths. It is fast and interpretable, but success does not establish multi-hop reasoning, aggregation, or realistic document understanding.

pairs.label: RULER
pairs.detail: Extends simple retrieval with multiple needles, tracing, and aggregation under configurable length and task complexity.
pairs.explanation: Extends simple retrieval with multiple needles, tracing, and aggregation under configurable length and task complexity. Its authors explicitly caution that synthetic tasks do not replace realistic evaluation.

pairs.label: HELMET
pairs.detail: Covers diverse application-centered categories at controlled lengths and reports that synthetic recall does not reliably predict every downstream behavior.
pairs.explanation: Covers diverse application-centered categories at controlled lengths and reports that synthetic recall does not reliably predict every downstream behavior.

pairs.label: LongBench v2
pairs.detail: Uses challenging long-context tasks spanning documents, dialogue, code repositories, in-context learning, and structured data.
pairs.explanation: Uses challenging long-context tasks spanning documents, dialogue, code repositories, in-context learning, and structured data. It broadens realism but still needs a product-specific release suite.

It varies input length, evidence position, task structure, distractors, and output requirements, then measures both answer quality and whether the answer is supported by the supplied context.
variants.prompt: A model API accepts 128K tokens. What does that fact establish by itself?
options: The model uses evidence equally well at every position through 128K.
The request can fit within the advertised input limit, but usable behavior still needs measurement.
The model will outperform retrieval at 128K.
Latency and cost will remain constant through 128K.
variants.explanation: An accepted input length is a transport and serving property. It does not prove retrieval, reasoning, evidence use, latency, or output quality across that window.

variants.prompt: A length-by-depth grid has strong average task success, but the 50% depth slice fails the predeclared evidence-use floor. What should the release gate do?
options: Pass because the average is strong.
Delete the middle slice and recompute the average.
Block or constrain the release until the failed critical slice is addressed.
Lower the floor after seeing the result.
variants.explanation: A predeclared slice floor prevents a strong average from hiding a known failure region. The supported operating frontier must exclude or repair that region.

variants.prompt: Why should a long-context test sweep evidence depth as well as context length?
options: To make every prompt contain the same number of tokens.
Because evidence position can change performance even when the total input length is unchanged.
Because middle-position evidence is always easier.
To eliminate the need for repeated trials.
variants.explanation: Position sensitivity can hide behind one aggregate score. A depth sweep exposes beginning, middle, and end behavior at the same length.

variants.prompt: When can retrieval-assisted context be preferable to sending every source token directly?
options: When retrieval recall, evidence preservation, and generation quality pass their own product-shaped gates.
Whenever the source collection contains more than one document.
Only when the model has no context window.
Because retrieval removes the need to evaluate grounding.
